sections: Comparing reload and recompute during the test wait

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Paused-State Policies** in *KV Cache Management* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, KV Cache Management, § Paused-State Policies
blocks.md: While the r18 repair request waits 45 seconds for its integration test suite (or whenever an agent blocks on an external tool or remote database), the model generates no tokens, yet retaining its KV cache in accelerator memory ties up scarce HBM. To prevent idle requests from starving active generation, the serving engine must execute a **paused-state policy**: retain the state in device memory, offload it to host memory or secondary storage, or drop it entirely and reconstruct it when the tool output arrives.

options: By Little's law a fixed pool of slots sustains a turn rate inversely proportional to residence, so holding state through a synchronous tool wait divides the memory-bound turn rate by 1 + T_tool/T_model.
During a tool wait the engine keeps, moves, or drops only uniquely reclaimable blocks, and offloading pays only when the wait exceeds the transfer round trip and memory is contested.
Splitting an uncached prompt into chunks under a per-iteration token budget bounds the inter-token gap of ongoing streams to one iteration at a modest delay to the new request's first token.
A reusable prefix must be compatible, available, and permitted, and none of the three says whether the evidence is current, so freshness is enforced by the harness rewriting the prompt.
